primary_meaning: The created expanse or vault of the heavens that separates the upper waters from the lower, embodying divine cosmic order and serving as the visible theater of God's glory

alternatives.meaning: A solid dome or firm vault (ancient Near Eastern cosmology) that holds back celestial waters and supports the heavenly bodies
The atmosphere or open sky (modern scientific accommodation), simply the air and space above the earth
Heaven as the transcendent dwelling-place or throne-room of God, mediating between earthly and divine realms
Allegorical figure for the Church, Scripture, or the firmament of faith that separates believers from worldly chaos
basis: Patristic readings of Genesis 1 and Psalm 19

notes: Christian tradition consistently treats the firmament first as the Genesis expanse that structures creation and secondarily as the heavens that declare God's glory; literal-solid, atmospheric, and purely heavenly readings coexist as complementary rather than mutually exclusive layers, while full allegorical mappings remain peripheral.
